items.q: Can GoHighLevel replace Jobber for quotes, invoices and payments?
items.a: For a small operation, GoHighLevel can handle the paperwork. HighLevel's help center describes estimates sent by email or text that the customer accepts or declines and that convert into an invoice, and payment runs through connected processors such as Stripe, PayPal and Square. HighLevel also documents a two-way QuickBooks integration. What GoHighLevel's published features leave out is the stretch between a signed estimate and the final invoice: crew scheduling, routing, job checklists, time tracking and job costing. Jobber is built around that stretch. Its Connect plan, $139 a month for one user on monthly billing when Jobber's pricing page was saved on 6 October 2026, adds automated client reminders, quote and invoice follow-ups and checklists, and its Grow plan adds job costing. A one-truck contractor quoting a few jobs a week can quote and bill in GoHighLevel. A company with several crews in the field should run the job itself in Jobber or another field-service tool.

items.q: Is GoHighLevel or Jobber cheaper for a one-person contractor?
items.a:
Jobber is cheaper to start. When Jobber's pricing page was saved on 6 October 2026, its Core plan cost $49 a month for one user on monthly billing, or $29 a month billed annually, and covered quotes, scheduling, invoices, online payments and a website. GoHighLevel's Starter plan costs $97 a month before usage, and CinchStack's solo bill, with 200 texts and 2,000 emails a month, comes to $103.51.

The order flips as features are added. On Jobber, automated client reminders start with Connect at $139 a month for one user, and two-way texting with Grow at $199, while GoHighLevel's Starter already includes two-way texting, missed-call text back and review requests, with the messages, phone number and A2P fees billed on top. A solo contractor who mainly needs to quote, schedule and bill should pick Jobber Core. One who mainly needs to answer every call and follow up every lead should pick GoHighLevel.

items.q: Do GoHighLevel and Jobber charge per user?
items.a:
GoHighLevel does not. Every GoHighLevel plan includes unlimited users and contacts, so the $97 Starter plan costs the same for an owner working alone as for a company where a dispatcher, three estimators and ten technicians all need logins.

Jobber prices by team size. Its pricing page, as saved on 6 October 2026, shows one-user prices for its Core, Connect and Grow plans, then separate tiers for 2 to 5 people, 6 to 10, 11 to 15, and 16 or more. The 2-to-5 tier includes 5 users, with Connect at $199 a month, Grow at $299 and Plus at $499 on monthly billing. For a growing crew, that structure matters more than the entry prices: Jobber's Connect costs $139 a month for one user but $199 for the 2-to-5 tier, and bigger teams move up to the larger tiers, while the GoHighLevel subscription stays at its plan price and only the usage charges grow with the business.

items.q: Does Jobber send review requests automatically?
items.a:
Yes, through Marketing Suite. Jobber's marketing page says Marketing Suite sends an automatic review request after every job and lets you answer new reviews with an AI-drafted or custom reply. It is an add-on listed at $99 a month on Jobber's pricing page, saved on 6 October 2026, and it comes bundled in the Plus plan for teams of 2 to 5. The same marketing page says a Jobber website and Google Business Profile optimization come with every Jobber plan at no extra cost.

GoHighLevel includes review requests in every plan once a Google Business Profile is connected, sent by text or email, by hand or from a workflow step, and bills the messages: $0.00747 per US text segment plus a carrier fee, or $0.675 per 1,000 emails. A contractor running both tools need not buy Marketing Suite for this: the Jobber marketplace listing for HighLevel's app says it can send review requests automatically once a job is completed.

items.q: Can GoHighLevel track calls from my Google Business Profile?
items.a:
Yes. HighLevel's help center describes a call-tracking switch for a connected Google Business Profile. Turning it on puts a LeadConnector number from your GoHighLevel account in the listing's primary phone slot, moves your existing number to the secondary slot and forwards calls to it, so calls to the listing's main number are logged in GoHighLevel. If nobody answers, Missed Call Text Back can text the caller from the tracking number.

HighLevel says moving a real number to the secondary slot has not been found to hurt rankings; that is HighLevel's own claim, so watch your listing's call volume after the change. Each forwarded call costs $0.02 a minute because both legs are billed, and the local number costs $1.15 a month. The text back also needs A2P 10DLC registration first: $22.50 once for a Sole Proprietor or Low Volume Standard brand, plus a campaign fee from $1.50 a month.

items.q: How do you connect GoHighLevel and Jobber?
items.a:
With HighLevel's own Jobber app, which Jobber's App Marketplace lists with HighLevel as the developer. HighLevel's help article describes a two-way client sync covering first and last name, email, phone, address, lead source, tags, the Jobber client link and the date the client was created. Jobber's custom fields, notes and attachments do not sync, and a Jobber account can be linked to only one GoHighLevel sub-account.

You pick a start date for importing past clients once, and it cannot be changed afterward; the sync cannot be paused, only disconnected from Jobber's side. The marketplace listing adds jobs and job updates to the sync choices and says review requests can go out automatically when a job is completed. The app is installed from the agency view of a GoHighLevel account, then connected inside the sub-account. Neither page lists a fee for the app, and the texts and emails its workflows send are billed at the usual rates.

items.q: How long does A2P 10DLC approval take before I can text customers from GoHighLevel?
items.a:
GoHighLevel's one-time A2P registration fee includes a $3 Fast Track charge aimed at approval within 3 business days, so plan on days rather than hours, and longer if the campaign is rejected. The fee is $22.50 for a Sole Proprietor or Low Volume Standard brand, and the monthly campaign fee starts at $1.50.

While a campaign shows Pending, HighLevel's campaign guide says not to create another campaign or resubmit. If it is rejected, open the required fixes, correct every item and resubmit; HighLevel's A2P fee article says a resubmission carries no new vetting fee. After approval, check that the sending number shows the A2P Verified label under Phone Numbers, because an approved campaign cannot carry texts until the number is linked to it. Getting the website right first saves a round trip: the guide asks for a live site with the business name and contact details, a privacy policy, terms and a clear description of how customers opt in.
